svg.title: Four resource walls in server scaling
svg.desc: A server must budget file descriptors, memory, CPU and scheduling work, and queued or in-flight requests. Each connection consumes resources even while idle.

g.text: Scale is a resource budget, not one magic setting
Multiply every per-connection cost by peak concurrency, then leave headroom for the rest of the process.
client sockets + upstream sockets + files + logs + pipes
Limits are per-process and system-wide; inspect them instead of
assuming 1024. A proxy may need two sockets per request.
socket buffers + application state + queues + stacks
Reserved virtual stack size is not always resident RAM, but large
thread counts still make memory and scheduling expensive.
parsing + TLS + application work + copies + context switches
System calls are only one cost. Too many runnable threads, cache
misses, lock contention, and callbacks also consume CPU.
accepted sockets + pending responses + application jobs
Longer service time holds resources longer. Bounded queues and
backpressure prevent overload from becoming memory growth.
Capacity is safe only when all four budgets remain below their limits together.
